answer: Run the identity registry like a harbor insurance market. Before an agent can earn, an underwriter must stake capital on it as its beacon of trust: if the agent is later proven to be one of many fakes run by the same operator, the underwriter's stake is slashed and paid to the network. Underwriters only insure agents they have audited, pricing premiums against the risk that a fleet of look-alikes appears on the horizon. A Sybil farmer cannot mint identities for free — each fake needs a sponsor willing to lose money on it, and insuring a thousand fakes costs more than they could ever extract.
